Zisha's Northern Song origin rests on one line of Mei Yaochen poetry ('紫泥新品泛春华') and Tian Zibing's own inference ('this reflects that Yixing was already producing zisha in the Northern Song'); no kiln site, dated vessel or stratigraphy is given, and the three-phase periodisation (Song start / Ming fame / Qing peak) has no intermediate material

Two parallel lists of zisha clays coexist (white-green-red by Tian Zibing; purple-red-yellow-white-black-flower by Xia Yanjing 2009) with no statement of their relation; proportions, shrinkage, firing curves and measured kiln temperatures are all absent, and 'over 1000 degrees' is the only temperature expression

Zisha master lists are mutually inconsistent: Tian Zibing gives both the Four Masters (Dong Han, Zhao Liang, Yuan Chang, Shi Peng) and Gongchun's three disciples (Shi Dabin, Zhao Liangbi, Chen Mingyuan), Li Lixin gives only the Four Masters, and Xia Yanjing 2009 lists Shi Dabin, Chen Mingyuan and 'Gongshou' together as Ming masters; no book explains the scope or basis of its list

Chen Mingyuan has three incompatible dates: Tian Zibing L4260 lists him as one of Gongchun's three disciples, L4595 places him in the Kangxi period, and Xia Yanjing 2016 lists him among Ming masters - the three are a century or more apart and no birth/death year or dated vessel settles it

Gongchun / Gongshou / Gongchun (龚春) coexist as three names: Xia Yanjing 2009 and 2016 write '供寿', Tian Zibing writes '供春' and records the original name '龚春'; whether these are variant writings of one person or two people is not stated

Zisha production organisation is entirely absent: no workshop, guild, imperial supply, export firm or apprenticeship system appears in the six books; 'about a dozen dragon kilns on Shushan firing zisha' is the only settlement-level description, with no kiln owners, workers or sales network. The modern three steps (resume production 1950, organise scattered craftsmen 1954, production cooperative 1955) give only years and institution names, no property or distribution arrangements

Gu Jingzhou and Gao Zhuang's 'Tibi tea set' collaboration is recorded in one sentence: Gao Zhuang's institutional identity, the division of design work, attribution and evaluation are all missing, so the only 'craftsman plus academy' case cannot serve as evidence for design-education history

Shiwan's Jun-imitative product carries three names (nijun by Tian Zibing, guangjun and foshajun by Xia Yanjing 2016) with no statement of whether they are synonyms or different periods/grades; glaze recipe, colouring mechanism and firing temperature are absent

Shiwan's origin and periodisation have no intermediate process: Xia Yanjing 2016 gives only 'Neolithic shell-mound sites already fired pottery' and 'large kilns appeared in the Tang', with no site names, dates or excavation data; Tian Zibing dates the distinctive character to 'modern times' while 2016 dates it to 'after entering the Qing', and the two periodisations are incompatible

Shiwan pottery sculpture has no named craftsman: the four famous pieces (Shouxian, Maitreya, golden toad, lucky lion) have only names, with no maker, date, dimension or collection; 'partly glazed, partly exposed body' is the only craft description, and the basis for choosing which parts to glaze is not recorded

The claim that Shiwan pottery art depended on bulk domestic pottery is the only economic-dependency judgement in the six books, but it has no output, value, employment or product-mix data behind it; the batch can only record it, not verify it

Rongchang is single-source (two passages in Tian Zibing): kiln count, output, firing temperature, clay composition, and the tools and sequence of iron-wire incising are all missing; 'two clays mixed into golden yellow' is a colour-mixing rather than a glaze statement and the proportion is unrecorded; 'pickle jars famous at home and abroad' is an evaluation, not sales data; Rongchang is now part of Chongqing while the source writes Sichuan

The four other 'five golden flowers' of Yixing (jun pottery, fine pottery, celadon, pottery sculpture) rest on a single passage (Tian Zibing L5083): Yixing jun pottery and Shiwan 'nijun' share a name but differ in substance and their relation is not discussed; whether Yixing 'fine pottery' and Shiwan 'fine pottery' are the same category is also unstated

Both caption-level objects (Ming melon-form teapot, Qing Dongling melon) have one caption line only, no visual verification of the plate, and no maker, dimension, collection or provenance; the referent of 'Dongling melon' (melon-form teapot or an ornamental vessel) is not explained in the source

The choice of three routes is an artefact of the record: the six books list seven other pottery regions (Jianshui, Qinxian, Jieshou, Tongguan, Macheng, Suiling, Luoyang) in one parallel sentence each with no KU entries; the batch does not expand from a single sentence, so 'three routes' is a sourcing boundary, not a material conclusion that modern pottery had only three routes
notes: 本批新建 1 个 Topic（B.5.5 泥胎装饰），挂载 11 个 KU，不新增 Theme。结构设计的三项判断：其一，原定 Topic 名「紫砂与明清陶器」是按材料加朝代命名，读完 11 条候选后改判为「泥胎装饰：紫砂、石湾与荣昌的三条路线」——材料回答的是瓷器占据主流之后陶器靠什么立身。其二，胎面三态：三条路线共同的不是「不用釉」，而是把装饰面从釉转回胎——宜兴全部露出（不挂釉，以泥色、造型与浅刻立身）、石湾露出一部分（部分上釉、局部露胎，以胎釉色差立身）、荣昌加工胎面（红白双色泥贴花嵌花、两色混合成金黄、铁线划花）。其三，师承承担制度史缺位时的位置：紫砂可追踪的关系只有师徒（供春—时大彬）、文人延揽（陈鸣远）、文人设计艺人制作（陈曼生—杨彭年的曼生壶）、艺人加学院（顾景舟与高庄）四种；紫砂有具名师承而石湾、荣昌无一位匠人姓名，这一不对称可能来自工艺水平也可能只来自文献选择，六册无法区分，故登记为记录问题而非工艺高低的证据。四处边界处置：石湾「泥钧」只取露胎的胎釉关系、釉料与烧成归 B.5.4；石湾「花釉瓷」不作材质判定；七处产陶区不据一句立条；紫砂当代产业组织与政策归 D。本批不 commit、不 push。
